purpose: Lets a user toggle a boolean choice or select one or more items from a list. The selection is held until the user submits or confirms — it does not trigger an immediate action. For a setting that takes effect instantly, use a Toggle instead.

props.name: label
props.description: The visible label beside the checkbox. Always required — a checkbox without a label is inaccessible.

props.name: checked
props.description: The checked state. Pass this to control the checkbox from outside.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Shows a dash instead of a tick. Means some but not all items in a related group are checked. Set only on a parent checkbox in a nested list — never as a default or loading state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the checkbox. Prefer hiding it or explaining why it is unavailable.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: When set, puts the checkbox into an error state and shows this message below. Use when the checkbox is required and unchecked on submit, e.g. terms and conditions.

variants.name: default
variants.whenToUse: Any time the user needs to make a boolean choice or select items from a list. The choice is applied later, on form submit.

variants.name: indeterminate
variants.whenToUse: Only on a parent checkbox that controls a group of child checkboxes, when some but not all children are checked. Never use as a default, placeholder, or loading state.

variants.name: error
variants.whenToUse: When the checkbox is required and the user has submitted without checking it. Always pair with an errorMessage explaining what is needed.

states.name: unchecked
states.description: Resting state. Empty box with strong border.

states.name: checked
states.description: Box filled with brand colour, white tick mark.

states.name: indeterminate
states.description: Box filled with brand colour, white dash. Represents partial selection in a group.

states.name: focus
states.description: Keyboard focus. Visible 2px focus ring using the focus-ring token.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Non-interactive. Box uses disabled surface and border tokens. Tick and dash use disabled text token.

states.name: error
states.description: Required checkbox left unchecked. Border uses error token, message shown below.

antiPatterns.never: Use indeterminate as a default, loading, or 'not yet decided' state.
antiPatterns.because: Indeterminate has one specific meaning: some but not all children in a controlled group are checked. Using it outside that context misrepresents the state to the user and to assistive technology.

antiPatterns.never: Use a Checkbox for a setting that takes immediate effect.
antiPatterns.because: A checkbox communicates a deferred choice — the selection is applied when the user submits or confirms. A setting that changes something instantly belongs in a Toggle, which communicates immediacy.

antiPatterns.never: Use a Checkbox when only one option can be selected from a group.
antiPatterns.because: Mutual exclusivity is what radio buttons communicate. A group of checkboxes implies multiple selections are valid. Using checkboxes for a single-answer question sets the wrong expectation.

antiPatterns.never: Omit an errorMessage when a required checkbox is left unchecked.
antiPatterns.because: A silent validation failure — the form won't submit but nothing explains why — is a dead end. The error message must say what is required and why.

keyboard: Tab moves focus to the checkbox
accessibility.focus: Visible 2px focus ring on :focus-visible using the focus-ring token, offset by 2px.
aria: aria-describedby points to the error message element when errorMessage is set
indeterminate state is set via the DOM property element.indeterminate — there is no HTML attribute equivalent
label is always associated via htmlFor/id and by wrapping — never rely on visual proximity alone
accessibility.contrast: Brand fill on white border meets WCAG AA 3:1 for UI components. Error red on white meets WCAG AA 4.5:1. Disabled mark on disabled surface meets WCAG AA 4.5:1.

examples: I agree to the terms and conditions
You must accept the terms to continue.

agentNotes: Use Checkbox for deferred boolean choices — terms, preferences, multi-select filters. Use Toggle for instant-effect settings. Use Radio for mutually exclusive options. When building a 'select all' pattern, set indeterminate on the parent only when some children are checked; set it to checked when all are checked and unchecked when none are. Never use indeterminate as a third value for a standalone checkbox.
